data.title: Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) Gains as a New Backed Company Prepares for IPO
data.description:
Chip stock Intel (INTC) has been making some exciting progress as a company lately. It turns out that it is also making exciting progress as a company backer. We heard about Kepler Computing yesterday, but one more came to the forefront in a report from Reuters. Altera is setting up for an initial public offering (IPO) that could be worth $2 billion to the company. That news reflected well on Intel, and shares rose over 3% in Friday afternoon's trading. Intel has seen a 316.61% rally in its share price over the past year.

Another Potential Winner

The report noted that Altera could be ready for its IPO before the end of this year, and would be one of the largest semiconductor listings of the last few years. Barclays is set to serve as underwriter for the IPO, but the order of the banks involved has not been finalized.

Better yet, it would also serve as reinforcement that the United States IPO market has been having a record year. The total IPO market stands at around $137 billion total raised through the end of August, and there are several other IPOs remaining that could emerge this year. Since Intel backed Altera before the IPO, it would likely receive a substantial portion of that release itself. Better yet, Altera makes a line of programmable chips currently in use in several fields, including the telecom market and the United States military.

If demand stays brisk—as it is likely to—and improved pricing accompanies this gain, it could be a very big win for Intel, and those who invest at this point.

data.title: PayPal's (PYPL) New CEO Chooses a Rebuild Over a Buyout
data.description:
PayPal's (PYPL) new CEO Enrique Lores is laying out a plan to rebuild the fintech company rather than sell it, WSJ reported. Lores, who stepped into the role about six months ago, seeks to overhaul slow‑moving parts of the business, launch new products, and cut billions in costs. His challenge remains tough competition in the digital payments market.

A key part of his strategy is turning Venmo into a full money‑management app. Venmo already offers crypto trading, debit and credit cards, and a stablecoin (PYUSD). PayPal plans to add budgeting tools, investing features, and a buy‑now‑pay‑later option.

Lores aims for Venmo to look more like SoFi (SOFI) or Chime, which blend payments with banking and investing. For PayPal's core checkout button, he plans to improve rewards and user experience to win back share from Apple (AAPL) Pay and Google (GOOGL) Wallet.

His plan comes as shareholders weigh what could have been a sale. Stripe and Advent International floated an offer around $60.50 a share, sending PayPal stock above $62 before talks stalled.

Key Pillars of PayPal's Turnaround Strategy

PayPal's turnaround plan includes $1.5 billion in cost cuts over the next two to three years by trimming layers and simplifying its products. The company is also rolling out AI tools to handle customer service and speed up how it builds and releases new products.

In April 2026, PayPal dropped its old corporate structure and moved to a simpler three‑unit model to cut overlap and speed up product launches. The new setup has three groups: Checkout Solutions & PayPal, Consumer Finance Services & Venmo, and Payments Services & Crypto.

Further, the company is using its strong cash position to fund a $6 billion share repurchase program to shore up earnings per share (EPS).

data.title: Target Stock (TGT) Looks Good Despite Doubts Over "Wildcard" Beauty Move
data.description:
Shares in retailer Target (TGT) edged higher today despite a leading analyst declaring that the jury was out on whether its new beauty business would help make its revenues more attractive.

Beauty Growth Uncertain

Five-star TipRanks-rated Oppenheimer analyst Rupesh Parikh said in a note today that Target's new Beauty Studio was visually appealing and well-curated, but whether it will translate to sales growth "remains a wildcard."

He said that initial store visits showed a bigger presence of skincare, haircare and K-Beauty relative to makeup. "We look forward to seeing how the assortment and experience evolves over time," the note said. He kept an Outperform rating on TGT stock and a price target of $180.

The new offering launched in more than 600 stores nationwide and online, including over 1,600 products from 90 prestige, emerging and global brands. Over two-thirds of the brands are new to Target, while more than 60% are also carried at specialty retailers Ulta Beauty (ULTA) and Sephora, Parikh said.

Demand Still Dazzles

Target introduced the Target Beauty Studio in March this year. It is designed as a new space within Target's beauty department to spotlight prestige beauty brands. This will help the retailer deepen its presence in a market estimated to be worth $36 billion in 2025.

"Backed by Target's merchandising authority and expertise in spotting what's next for guests, the new space combines curated discovery, personalized expertise and an elevated experience that's designed to help guests discover the latest trends, innovations and must-have products across makeup, skincare, haircare, fragrance and more," Target explained at the time.

According to recent figures from Circana, prestige beauty sales reached $17.1 billion during the first six months of 2026, up 7% year on year, while mass-market beauty sales rose at the same rate to $39.2 billion. Fragrance and skincare emerged as the strongest-performing categories, which revealed that despite consumer confidence uncertainty people are still keen to spend on looking their best.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Gains as it Hits Phase 2 of U.S. Army's IFPC Program
data.description:
Aerospace stock Boeing (BA) made some gains today, as it, along with Anduril, advanced to the second phase of the United States Army's Indirect Fire Protection Capability (IFPC) Increment 2 interceptor program. Now, the competition is down to Boeing/Anduril and Lockheed Martin (LMT) to see who lands the contract. That was good news to investors, and Boeing shares were up nearly 3% in Friday afternoon's trading. Boeing has seen a 5.16% loss in its share price over the past year.

Closer to the Win

Boeing is now part of the "demonstration phase" of the development operation, noted a representative from the Army, who also noted that there would be more information released about the competition when it was "…appropriate."

The IFPC Increment 2 program is intended to serve as a step between short-range defensive operations and long-range defenses like the Patriot missile system. Boeing revealed that its entry into the program brought together "…seeker technology, a compact form factor, a solid rocket motor supplied by Anduril Rocket Motor Systems and a Modular Open Systems Architecture."

Meanwhile, Boeing also introduced us to an employee who celebrated a milestone of his own, becoming the longest-serving employee in the company's history. That honor belongs to Charlie Tapper, a 96-year-old man who has been employed by Boeing for 75 years, and has absolutely no plan to retire. Tapper signed on with Boeing in 1951, just a week after getting a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from Oregon State University. Tapper's engineering credits include work on the LGM-30 Minuteman missile and testing of the first automatically deploying slides on the 747.

data.title: September Rate Hike Odds Surge Above 85%as Inflation Accelerates
data.description:
Rate hike odds at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting surged on Friday after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) published August's Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. During the month, the CPI rose 0.4%, up from 0.1% in July. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy items, advanced 0.3% compared to 0.2% in the prior month.

The odds of a 25-basis-point hike next week are now at 88.7%, up from 72.4% on Thursday and 59.4% a week ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

Fed Faces Balancing Act as Inflation Stays Elevated

Inflation has remained above the Fed's 2% target for over five years. Higher rates can help ease inflation by increasing borrowing costs and discouraging consumers and companies from spending.

data.title: Oracle Stock (ORCL) Erases Earlier Gains and Falls After Earnings
data.description:
The post-earnings bounce in Oracle's (ORCL) stock was short-lived. In early afternoon trading on Sept. 11, ORCL stock had given up an earlier 6% gain and turned negative as investors and analysts consider the company's latest financial results. In afternoon trading, Oracle's shares were down 1% with downside pressure appearing to build on the stock heading into the weekend.

ORCL stock appeared to be headed for a nice gain on the day after the technology giant reported better-than-expected financial results and raised its guidance. The company posted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.92, which beat the $1.74 consensus expectation of Wall Street. Revenue totaled $19.35 billion, which topped the $19.14 billion that had been forecast on Wall Street. Sales were up 30% from a year earlier.

Oracle's Deteriorating Finances

Unfortunately, the strong print does not appear to have been enough to overcome other challenges that Oracle is experiencing, namely with its finances. Oracle, which is mostly known for its software products, is pivoting to artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. However, Oracle is in a weaker cash position and has a lower credit rating than the hyperscalers it is competing against in the data center space.

The deteriorating finances have pressured Oracle's share price. ORCL stock has declined 48% over the last 12 months.

data.title: HP Stock (HPQ) Soars Despite RBC Capital's Hold Rating — Here's Why
data.description:
Shares in PC maker HP Inc. (HPQ) jumped by 7% to around $35 per share on Friday afternoon. This came despite a new Hold rating from RBC Capital's five-star analyst David Paige. The rally followed bullish comments on product demand for PC rival Dell Technologies (DELL). DELL stock jumped by 11% to $563.

Why RBC Capital Is Cautious of HP

On August 26, HP released its fiscal Q3 2026 earnings. The PC maker's revenue came in at a record $15.7 billion, up by 12.5% from last year.

Its earnings per share also rose by roughly 11% to $0.83, aided by a $0.11 boost from government tariff refunds. However, the California-based company flagged profit pressure on its Personal Systems segment, its biggest business division.

data.title: Chewy Stock (CHWY) Falls 5% on Downgrade from JPMorgan Chase
data.description:
Shares of pet product retailer Chewy (CHWY) are down 5% after the stock received a downgrade and price target cut from JPMorgan Chase (JPM). Analysts Margaret Hoffman and Doug Anmuth downgraded CHWY stock to a Hold-equivalent neutral rating from a Buy-equivalent overweight rating previously. They also and cut their price target on the shares to $24 from $29.

The new price target is 14% higher than where the stock currently trades. In a note to clients, the analysts cited continued macroeconomic pressures and muted organic growth as reasons for the downgrade to Chewy stock. The lowered rating and price target cut come after Chewy recently reported disappointing financial results.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: Vicor Stock (VICR) Soars 11% on New Manufacturing Site Acquisitions
data.description:
Vicor (VICR) stock was up 11.13% on Friday after the modular power components and systems maker announced new acquisitions in a press release. The company said it is buying a 334,000-square-foot building on 66 acres in Merrimack, New Hampshire.

It is also buying 54 acres in nearby Hooksett. The two sites will support Vicor's ChiP Fab-2 and Fab-3. Together, the fabs are set to have nearly one million square feet of space. The move comes as use of ChiP Fab-1 in Andover, Massachusetts, nears its current limit.

ChiP Fab-1 has been built out to 320,000 square feet on 16 acres. The new sites will let Vicor add much more capacity as demand for AI hardware grows. The company said ChiP Fab-2 could be ready for its first use within about one year. The added space is meant to give OEMs and large cloud companies more room to scale their AI systems.

How Vicor's Tech Can Help AI Data Centers

Vicor noted that its Vertical Power Delivery technology can help solve power limits tied to older voltage tools. The company also said that its tech can deliver the power needed by advanced AI systems. It also sees the new fabs as a way to give customers a U.S. source for key power parts. That could help firms that face supply risks or need a clear path to use Vicor tech.

According to the company, this expansion will add to its ability to serve the AI hardware market from more than one ChiP fab. The company said this can help make supply more steady as AI systems grow more complex. Vicor also plans to keep using its tech license model as it adds new fab capacity. The goal is to give OEMs and large cloud companies more supply choice and a clear path to use its power tech.
